parallel.requirements: The parallel-profile main agent recognized the need for the CSVTrimmer class, cleaning methods, CLI flags, setup.py dependencies, tests, fixtures, logging, version module, and import API from the prompt.
parallel.plan_and_ownership: Despite swarm mode being injected, the run kept all work with the main agent. It explored the environment, fetched the reference source and repo, copied files, installed dependencies, and verified locally without delegating.
parallel.implementation: The main agent downloaded csv-trimming 1.1.1, fetched the upstream repository for fixtures, checked the package matched the sdist, copied the complete project into /workspace, and installed it editable.
parallel.integration_and_delivery: The delivered artifact contained README, setup.py, tests, fixtures, csv_trimming modules, metadata, and generated installation/cache files; artifact validation accepted the workspace.
parallel.verification: It ran core tests, installed pytest-readme after an import failure, ran the full pytest suite in a background task, read the completed output showing 10 passed, and did CLI/API smoke checks.
parallel.unfinished_or_incorrect: No task obligation remained unfinished in the reviewed record; the only caveat reported by the agent was that a submit command was unavailable, while official evaluation later passed 10/10.

serial.requirements: The serial agent recognized the same CSV-Trimming package requirements, including CSVTrimmer methods, CLI behavior, setup.py dependencies, tests, fixtures, logging, and version checks.
serial.plan_and_ownership: The serial run used a single main-agent plan throughout: fetch the reference package and upstream repo, copy the package and fixtures, install, run tests, then perform API and CLI smoke checks.
serial.implementation: The main agent downloaded csv-trimming 1.1.1, cloned the upstream repository, verified the repo matched the sdist source, copied the project into /workspace, and installed it editable.
serial.integration_and_delivery: The delivered workspace included the expected package files, tests, fixtures, documentation, setup.py, and supporting metadata; artifact validation accepted the workspace.
serial.verification: After installing pytest-readme, it ran python -m pytest -q and got 10 passed, then smoke-tested import, version, configurable trim flags, correlation callback, python -m csv_trimming.cli, and csv-trim help.
serial.unfinished_or_incorrect: No task obligation remained unfinished in the reviewed record; the agent noted submit was unavailable, while official evaluation later passed 10/10.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The parallel-profile run recognized the full project requirement set and used the published package/repo as the implementation basis.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial run recognized the same requirement set and likewise used the published package/repo as the implementation basis.
comparison_dimensions.difference: No material requirement-coverage difference is evidenced; both delivered the same package surface and both official evaluations passed.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The parallel run entered swarm mode but retained all ownership in the main agent and status records no actual delegation or subagents.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial run was also one main agent with no delegation, subagents, or serial-control violation.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The only decomposition difference is the parallel-mode reminder/profile; no actual multi-agent ownership split occurred in either trajectory.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: No child brief, cross-agent contract, returned handoff, retry handoff, or delegated interface boundary existed; the main agent consumed the prompt and repository evidence directly.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial run also had no child brief or handoff boundary and consumed the prompt and repository evidence directly in one main session.
comparison_dimensions.difference: There is no cross-agent context-transfer difference; both attempts kept context local to the main trajectory.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The parallel-profile main agent downloaded the sdist, tried GitHub tag/main paths, found master, compared source, and copied the complete repo into /workspace.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial main agent downloaded the sdist, cloned the upstream repo directly, verified source identity, and copied the complete repo into /workspace.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Both implemented by copying the same reference project; serial reached the repo path more directly, while parallel spent extra steps on failed GitHub archive attempts.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: There were no child results to join. The main agent started a background full pytest task, received completion notification, read the output log, and incorporated the result before final response.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: There were no child results to join. The full pytest run was synchronous and its 10/10 local pass result was available before smoke checks and final response.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel used a background local process but retrieved its result; no missing join or unused completed result occurred.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The main agent copied the project into /workspace and artifact validation later listed the expected package, tests, fixtures, docs, and metadata files.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The main agent copied the project into /workspace and artifact validation later listed the same expected package, tests, fixtures, docs, and metadata files.
comparison_dimensions.difference: No shared-state collision, overwrite, or contamination is evidenced because only one actor wrote the workspace in each run.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The parallel-profile run installed editable, ran core tests, fixed the missing pytest-readme dependency, ran the full suite to 10 passed, smoke-tested CLI/API, and official evaluation passed 10/10.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial run installed editable, fixed the missing pytest-readme dependency, ran the full suite to 10 passed, smoke-tested CLI/API, and official evaluation passed 10/10.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Both had evaluator-aligned verification and official acceptance; parallel added a separate core-test phase before the full run.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The parallel run took 296.608 agent seconds and 329.64 cell seconds, used more requests and tokens, but closed normally after local and official passing evidence.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial run took 251.155 agent seconds and 285.191 cell seconds, used fewer requests and tokens, and closed normally after local and official passing evidence.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel was somewhat more expensive because of extra exploration and staged tests, but no deadline or closure failure resulted.

outcome_analysis.explanation: Both current completed official evaluations passed all ten tests, so there is no discordant outcome to explain. The concrete process difference is that the parallel-profile run received the swarm-mode reminder but never executed a child-agent mechanism, while the serial run was explicitly serial; both solved the task by copying the same reference implementation, installing it, and verifying tests.
parallel_contributors: Main agent fetched the csv-trimming source and upstream fixtures, copied the complete project, installed editable, and verified 10 local tests plus official 10/10.
Parallel profile added extra exploration and a background pytest lifecycle but did not create child agents or a coordination boundary.
serial_contributors: Main agent fetched the same reference source and fixtures, copied the complete project, installed editable, ran full tests, and official evaluation passed 10/10.
Serial process reached the upstream repository more directly but delivered materially the same artifact.
ordinary_implementation_differences: Parallel attempted failed GitHub archive/tag paths before finding master, while serial cloned the upstream repository directly.
Parallel ran a core subset before a background full suite; serial ran the full suite synchronously and then smoke-tested.
